title: Temu and Italy's ICQRF Partner to Strengthen Protection of Geographical Indications Online
summary:
- On Oct. 5, 2026, Temu and Italy's Central Inspectorate for Fraud Repression and Quality Protection of Agri-Food Products (ICQRF) signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen protection of Geographical Indications (GIs) on Temu's marketplace. The agreement, signed at an event marking ICQRF's 40th anniversary, emphasizes prevention, with the two parties to provide sellers with information and guidance and meet periodically to develop joint initiatives.
- Temu introduced a dedicated GI category within its global Brand Registry. Rights holders and authorised agents can register GI rights for Temu's review and, once approved, report potentially infringing listings through Temu's Brand Protection Center. A Temu spokesperson said the agreement combines prevention, information, guidance, and "effective mechanisms for addressing potential infringements."
- Dr. Felice Assenza, Head of Department at ICQRF, called the agreement "another key milestone" in ICQRF's strategy to protect GIs in international digital markets and said Temu has shown "a genuine willingness to engage in dialogue and cooperation." The agreement also sets up dedicated points of contact for regulatory clarification, practical issues, and coordinating monitoring of activities under the MoU.

title: Temu Introduces New GI Protection Feature to Support Local Producers
summary:
- On Oct. 1, 2026, Temu added a dedicated geographical indications (GI) category to its Brand Registry Portal, available across all markets. According to the press release, it lets rightsholders submit notifications of potential GI infringements for review.
- Temu said the GI feature is among its latest measures for businesses, drawing on feedback from more than 100 meetings with trade associations, chambers of commerce and start-up networks across Europe, where complexity emerged as a recurring barrier. A Temu spokesperson said the aim is "practical tools that reduce complexity."
- According to Temu's 2026 Intellectual Property Protection Report, its proactive monitoring database covers more than 15,000 brands, and proactive removals of potentially infringing listings outnumbered reactive takedowns by 331 to 1 during the reporting period. The company also said it works directly with more than 3,000 brands through its Brand Guardian Initiative.

title: Digest: McDonald’s Bets on $1bn Ad Business; Temu Cuts Fake Influencer Network on Meta
summary:
- Temu has quietly dismantled a nearly USD$1bn (£750m) network of suspected fake influencer accounts on Meta's platforms, which had been funding partnership ads targeting audiences in the UK and all 27 EU countries.
- According to Online Risk Labs, a Czech research group that examined 16 months of Temu's advertising activity through April 2026, roughly 73 of the 100 accounts featuring the most Temu ads were likely fake. Those 100 accounts ran more than 1.4 million partnership ads, reaching a combined audience of nearly 17 billion views.
- Within days, 90 of the flagged accounts stopped running Temu ads entirely, and total partnership ad volume from the company nearly halved. Neither Temu nor Meta responded to requests for comment.

title: Temu axed its $1 billion network of fake influencer accounts on Meta
summary:
- **Fake influencer network:** Online Risk Labs (ORL), a Czech-based social media research group, found that Temu had spent nearly $1 billion funding partnership ads with influencers and creators on Instagram and Facebook, targeting the U.K. and all 27 EU countries. ORL said around 73 of the 100 influencers with the most Temu ads were probably fake.

- **Reduced spending after Fortune's report:** Fortune first exposed the network in a story published Aug. 31, when Temu was running 4,900 partnership campaigns a day. Temu "appears to have largely stopped" funding it, according to the article. By Sept. 4, 90 accounts featured zero Temu advertising, and ORL said the overall number of partnership ads run by Temu almost halved.

- **Unexplained country-level drop:** ORL said partnership ads in Ireland, Cyprus, Austria, Denmark, Latvia, and Slovenia ceased almost entirely, but it is not clear why. Neither Temu nor Meta responded to requests for comment.

title: TEMU PARTNERS WITH CITEA TO SUPPORT CYPRUS' DIGITAL BUSINESS COMMUNITY
summary:
- On Sept. 16, 2026, Temu signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Cyprus Information Technology Enterprises Association (CITEA) to support Cyprus' technology and business community. Under the partnership, Temu will work with CITEA's programmes, events, and member companies, and the two organisations will collaborate on shared communications to showcase opportunities for local merchants.
- The partnership builds on Temu's Local Seller Program, which it introduced in Cyprus in 2025 to give eligible local businesses access to digital commerce opportunities and the potential to reach customers across Europe.
- CITEA President George Malekkos said that partnering with Temu gives CITEA members "greater visibility and access to European markets." A Temu spokesperson said the collaboration "gives us a direct line to help local businesses embrace digital channels, tap into international demand, and thrive across new markets."

title: China's Temu may have spent as much as $962 millionon Meta ads in the UK and Europe, with 73 of its top 100 creators likely fake
summary:
- **Fake creator accounts:** Online Risk Labs (ORL) research found that 73 of the 100 creators whose content Temu boosted most heavily across the UK and Europe were likely fake. Only eight were verified as real identities, 28 were based in Russia, 19 in China, and six in the EU or UK.
- **Top creator and spending estimate:** ORL says Ya Lili, Temu's top creator for partnership ads on Meta platforms in the UK and Europe, almost certainly does not represent a real person. Temu-boosted posts from the account were viewed more than 1 billion times across Facebook and Instagram in the 16 months ending April 2026. ORL estimates Temu spent as much as $962 million on similar ads across the UK and 27 EU countries during that period, based on total impressions and average cost per reach.
